key_insight: Patterned, compressively stressed TiN films could enable large deterministic valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots by inducing shear strain.
engineering_relevance: Integrating stressors with gate architectures offers a fabrication-compatible route toward more reproducible silicon spin-qubit arrays.
method: Model patterned stressed TiN films using finite-element simulations.
Combine induced shear strain with oscillatory Ge concentration in the quantum well.
Evaluate strain coverage across multiple dots and realistic gate geometries.
evidence_signal: Simulations predict quantum-well shear strains exceeding 0.1%, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of μeV, with strain maintained across multiple dots and realistic gate geometries.
watch_item: Experimental validation is needed to confirm that fabricated stressor-gate structures deliver the predicted strain and valley splitting reproducibly.
paper_title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
